name: proxy-admin
label: ProxyAdmin
shape: Self-administered: its admin slot is itself, so the walk leaves through owner() into an L1 alias

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0x4200..0018 (itself). owner() = 0x8cC5..6a6d, which has no code on Base; minus 0x1111..1111 it is 0x7bB4..595c, which has code on Ethereum and answers getThreshold()=2 over getOwners() = [0x9855..46a1 (3-of-6 Safe), 0x20Ac..A4Dd (8-of-11 Safe)]. All 17 inner owners have no code on Ethereum. Cheapest route: 3 + 8 = 11 keys.

name: l2-standard-bridge
label: L2StandardBridge
shape: The headline: a predeploy whose ProxyAdmin is owned by an L1 contract through its L2 alias

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation slot set, admin slot = ProxyAdmin 0x4200..0018; from there the same walk as the proxy-admin row: alias 0x8cC5..6a6d -> 2-of-2 Safe 0x7bB4..595c on Ethereum over a 3-of-6 and an 8-of-11 Safe of EOAs.

name: l1-message-sender
label: L1MessageSender (legacy predeploy)
shape: AdminOnly: admin slot set, implementation never set, still a live upgrade authority

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation slot zero, admin slot = 0x4200..0018, so whoever controls the ProxyAdmin can point it anywhere. Same root as the proxy-admin row.

name: usdbc
label: USDbC
shape: An m-of-n Safe as the direct admin (3-of-6 over EOAs)

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0xd94E..f94f, a Safe answering getThreshold()=3 over 6 owners; every owner has no code on Base and none at its unaliased address on Ethereum. Five of the six signers also sit on the 3-of-6 Safe 0x9855..46a1 behind the predeploys.

name: proxy-admin-under-safe
label: Unlabelled transparent proxy
shape: A ProxyAdmin owned by a Safe: the root is the Safe, not the immediate admin

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0x9CAA..755B, which answers owner() = 0x920F..7377 and reverts on the Safe and Timelock probes. 0x920F..7377 is a Safe, getThreshold()=3 over 5 owners, none with code on Base or at their unaliased Ethereum address.

name: eoa-admin
label: Unlabelled transparent proxy
shape: A genuine single key: the admin has no code on Base and none behind its alias on Ethereum

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0x0000..C000, no code on Base; its unaliased address 0xeeef..aeef has no code on Ethereum, so no L1 contract can act as it. One key.

name: unknown-admin
label: Unlabelled transparent proxy
shape: Expected Unknown: the admin has code and answers none of the probes

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0x31e9..0c17, 15,609 bytes of code; getOwners(), getThreshold(), owner() and getMinDelay() all return empty data. Nothing recognized, so the honest answer is no root. Its bytecode's selectors decode to a trading contract (getAllTesseraPools(), swapAmount(...), killContract()) with a bespoke multiSigOwner() getter; nothing establishes that getter gates upgrades, so it is not guessed at.

name: usd-plus
label: USD+
shape: UUPS confirmed, gated by OpenZeppelin AccessControl rather than an owner, and the role's holders are not listed on chain

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation slot = 0xe120..3cfD, admin and beacon slots zero. The implementation answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 implementation slot, so upgrades are UUPS and run through the proxy. Through the proxy, owner(), getOwners(), getThreshold() and getMinDelay() all revert: upgrades are gated by something other than an owner, so no root is expected. Re-read 2026-09-30 at the same block: supportsInterface(0x7965db0b) = true and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE() = 0, so it is OpenZeppelin AccessControl; UPGRADER_ROLE() and getRoleMemberCount(0) revert, so upgrades take the admin role and its holders are not enumerable. The root is the contract's own role, keys unknown.

name: uups-owner
label: Unlabelled UUPS proxy
shape: UUPS resolved through owner(): confirmed UUPS, root found, capped at Medium

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation slot = 0x4d5B..8e84, admin and beacon slots zero. The implementation answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 implementation slot. Through the proxy, owner() = 0xb045..7adb, which has no code on Base; its unaliased address 0x9f34..69ca has no code on Ethereum. One key, but only Medium: answering owner() does not prove owner() is what _authorizeUpgrade checks. The same key is owner() of two more UUPS proxies in the index.

name: uups-unconfirmed
label: Unlabelled implementation-slot proxy
shape: Implementation slot and no admin, but the implementation denies being UUPS

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation slot = 0xA4Ab..dFdB, admin and beacon slots zero. proxiableUUID() on the implementation reverts, so nothing establishes that upgrade logic lives there; the proxy itself answers none of the probes. No root is expected, and the reason is named rather than guessed.

name: beacon-proxy
label: Unlabelled beacon proxy
shape: Beacon: the root is whoever controls the beacon, shared here by five proxies

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation and admin slots zero, beacon slot = 0x0000..b2dc (836 bytes of code). The beacon answers owner() = 0xc509..39aa and reverts on the Safe and Timelock probes. 0xc509..39aa is a Safe, getThreshold()=2 over 3 owners, none with code on Base or at their unaliased Ethereum address.

name: usdc
label: USDC
shape: Not covered: the pre-1967 ZeppelinOS slot, kept to keep coverage honest

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. All ERC-1967 slots zero; keccak256('org.zeppelinos.proxy.implementation') holds 0x2Ce6..d779. Recorded, not covered.

name: weth9
label: WETH9
shape: Not upgradeable: code present, every slot empty

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. 2,041 bytes of code; implementation, admin, beacon and ZeppelinOS slots all zero.

name: sep29-before
label: Beacon proxy, before
shape: The largest root on 2026-09-20: one key behind a shared beacon, the block before it handed the beacon to a Safe

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes, found by bisecting owner() between the Sep 20 and Sep 29 scans. Beacon slot = 0xe68E..7706; implementation and admin slots zero. The beacon reverts getOwners/getThreshold/getMinDelay and answers owner() = 0x21eb..B5fc, which has no code on Base; unaliased (0x10da..a4eb) it has no code on Ethereum at 26,079,703 either. One key.

name: sep29-after
label: Beacon proxy, after
shape: The same proxy one block later: a root that changed hands, which only history can show

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes, one block later. Same beacon; owner() = 0x6454..Bf15, which has code, reverts owner()/getMinDelay and answers getThreshold() = 2 over five getOwners(). All five owners have no code on Base, and none of their unaliased addresses has code on Ethereum at 26,079,703. The previous owner, 0x21eb..B5fc, is one of the five. Two keys.

name: eip7702-self
label: EIP-7702 account
shape: An externally owned account that delegated its code (EIP-7702) and so reads as a UUPS proxy: its own key is the authority

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. getCode = 0xef0100 || 0x7702cb55..176c, a 23-byte EIP-7702 designator, so this is an EOA with delegated code. Implementation slot = 0x0001..9e72 (Coinbase Smart Wallet), admin and beacon zero; the implementation answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 slot. The account answers entryPoint() and nothing else Hermes probes, but its private key signs for it whatever the delegate allows. One key; Medium because the walk starts at a UUPS proxy.

name: eip7702-behind-admin
label: ProxyAdmin under an EIP-7702 key
shape: A ProxyAdmin whose owner is an EIP-7702 delegated EOA, one of two such keys behind 25 indexed proxies each

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0x7cfd..3b85, which reverts getOwners/getThreshold/getMinDelay/entryPoint and answers owner() = 0x7fa6..d27c. That address's code is 0xef0100 || 0x63c0..e32b, an EIP-7702 designator: an EOA with delegated code, so one key. Before model 2 it answered entryPoint() and was reported unrecognized.

name: multi-owner-account
label: UUPS proxy owned by a smart account
shape: A UUPS proxy whose owner() is a MultiOwnable smart account (Coinbase Smart Wallet): any one of its signers upgrades it

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation 0x6c85..d1e7 answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 slot; the proxy answers owner() = 0x2e93..e9aa. That account has 61 bytes of code, answers entryPoint() = 0x5FF1..2789 (EntryPoint v0.6) and nextOwnerIndex() = 2; ownerAtIndex(0) and (1) are 32-byte addresses 0x39a0..2bfa and 0xe6e9..8397, both without code on Base or at their unaliased address on Ethereum. MultiOwnable accepts any one owner, so one key; Medium for both the UUPS start and the account.

name: unread-account
label: Smart account, scheme unread
shape: A UUPS proxy that is itself an ERC-4337 account of a scheme Hermes does not read: a real root with no key count

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation 0x0000..b25a answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 slot. The proxy reverts owner/getOwners/getThreshold/getMinDelay, answers entryPoint() = 0x0000..a032 (EntryPoint v0.7) and reverts nextOwnerIndex(): an account whose signers are not listed in a way Hermes reads.

name: role-admin-holder
label: AccessControl, upgrade role empty
shape: An AccessControlEnumerable contract whose UPGRADER_ROLE has no holder, but whose admin role does: that holder can grant itself the upgrade

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation 0x2da3..86a1 answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 slot. The proxy reverts owner/getOwners/getThreshold/getMinDelay/entryPoint; supportsInterface(0x7965db0b) = true, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE() = 0, UPGRADER_ROLE() = 0x189a..d2e3 with getRoleMemberCount = 0. getRoleAdmin(UPGRADER_ROLE) = 0, getRoleAdmin(0) = 0, and role 0 has one member, 0x5393..09b2, with no code on Base or at its unaliased address on Ethereum. That key can grant itself UPGRADER_ROLE: one key.

name: renounced-to-sentinel
label: UUPS proxy, owner renounced
shape: A UUPS proxy whose owner() is 0xff..ff: a root no one holds a key for, not one key

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Implementation 0x0c70..8412 answers proxiableUUID() with the ERC-1967 slot. The proxy answers owner() = 0xff..ff (and also entryPoint(), which the walk never reaches because owner() answered first). No one can hold the key to 0xff..ff; before model 2 this ranked as a one-key EOA.

name: timelock-72h
label: ProxyAdmin under a 72h timelock
shape: A ProxyAdmin owned by a TimelockController: the delay is read, the proposer and executor roles are not listed on chain

checked.how: Raw JSON-RPC outside Hermes. Admin slot = 0xdf3f..78d0, which answers owner() = 0xf425..155a. That contract answers getMinDelay() = 0x3f480 = 259,200 s (72h), reverts owner/getOwners/getThreshold, answers supportsInterface(0x7965db0b) = true and reverts getRoleMemberCount(PROPOSER_ROLE): OpenZeppelin TimelockController, roles not enumerable.
